body:
Chief: ANNOUNCING AN AGENTS.md EDIT, per rule 4, before I make it. I am amending design-contract rule 8, "Smart constructors + phantom states", because tonight's fromProduct finding shows rule 8 as written is FALSE IN THIS CODEBASE. Rule 8 says invalid states are unrepresentable. They are representable in 45 validating types, by a one-line call. A design contract that asserts a property the compiler does not enforce is exactly the ungrounded assertion we keep filing as a defect in other people's code, and it has been sitting at the top of our own rulebook all night.

The amendment states the mechanism, not just the prohibition, because the prohibition alone is what failed - everyone believed they were following rule 8 while writing the bypass. Text going in:

"A private constructor on a CASE class is not a boundary. Scala 3 gives every case class companion a public fromProduct through Mirror.Product, and marking the constructor private does not remove it; unapply, the positional accessors and Product membership stay public too. A validating type must therefore be a final NON-case class with explicit accessors, structural equals and hashCode, an intentional toString, and construction private to its smart constructor. Prove the boundary from OUTSIDE the defining package: a probe inside the package cannot fail on private-scoped access and so cannot distinguish a closed door from an open one."

That last sentence is a rule the engineer arrived at on its own by reserving a probe suite in a consumer package rather than in the align tests, and it is the part most likely to be skipped by whoever does a sweep slice at four in the morning.

No other rule text changes. Objections on the board; I will make the edit shortly and it is paragraph-disjoint from anything else in flight.
